headline: Dry weather through Tuesday afternoon gives the best Sierra travel window before a weak storm brings light pass-level snow and ridgetop gusts up to 80 mph Tuesday night into Wednesday, while Thanksgiving looks dry and mild and the Mammoth Lakes area should stay dry all week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Freezing fog is possible early Monday in northeast California and eastern Sierra valleys, including along I-80 near Truckee, with low visibility and slick roads for the morning commute before the fog clears around 9 to 10 AM. After that, Monday and Monday night are dry and cool under high pressure, including around Mammoth Lakes and the rest of Mono County, with high clouds increasing in the afternoon.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Tuesday stays dry through the afternoon, the best window for crossing the Sierra before a weak storm brings snow showers from Lassen County to the Tahoe Basin Tuesday evening into Wednesday morning. Expect up to an inch of snow along the Sierra crest and at pass level, with only a 10 percent chance of 2 to 4 inches on the highest peaks and Donner Pass by midday Wednesday; Truckee and Tahoe have a 10 percent chance of a trace on grass. Mono County, including Mammoth Lakes, and western Nevada should stay dry, sheltered by the mountains. Winds pick up Tuesday afternoon, with southwest gusts of 25 to 35 mph near the Oregon border, 20 to 30 mph in eastern Sierra valleys, and up to 80 mph on ridgetops, making for rough backcountry and lake conditions and bumpy flights into Wednesday morning.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thanksgiving Day looks dry and mild under high pressure, aside from a 10 to 20 percent chance of rain near the Oregon border, with highs in the upper 40s and 50s and lows in the 20s and 30s early Friday. Friday and most of Saturday stay dry before another, warmer storm becomes more likely Sunday into Monday, with snow in the mountains and rain in the valleys, which could affect post-holiday travel. Computer models suggest a stormy pattern continuing into next week, but confidence is low that far out.

watch_for: Freezing fog and slick roads Monday morning near Truckee and in other eastern Sierra valleys until about 9 to 10 AM.
Tuesday night into Wednesday morning: up to an inch of snow at Sierra pass level, gusty winds and ridgetop gusts up to 80 mph.
A warmer storm possible Sunday into Monday that could affect post-holiday travel.
confidence: Forecasters are confident the midweek storm will be weak and that Thanksgiving will be dry, and have low confidence in the details of the stormy pattern late this weekend and into next week.
